description: Execution environment for Assignment 4 (distributed dense matmul, PySpark standalone)

cpu.hybrid_note: Intel i7-1355U: 2 P-cores (2 threads each, CPU0-3) + 8 E-cores (1 thread each, CPU4-11); 12 logical CPUs

windows_fixes: hostname VIVOBOOK_ALED is not a valid Spark URL host -> driver binds/advertises 127.0.0.1
Windows App Execution Alias for 'python' prints the Store banner and exits -> PYSPARK_PYTHON points at the real interpreter path
SPARK_LOCAL_IP=127.0.0.1 so worker daemons bind loopback

hadoop_helpers.why: Spark's event log is written through Hadoop's LocalFileSystem; on Windows that path needs %HADOOP_HOME%\bin\winutils.exe. Fetched by scripts/fetch_winutils.py into build/hadoop/ (git-ignored third-party binaries).
hadoop_helpers.scope_note: Only Hadoop FileSystem calls need it; matrix I/O in this study uses plain numpy file I/O.

cluster.topology_note: 1 driver process + 1 master process + N worker processes (1 JVM each, 1 core each), all bound to 127.0.0.1 on a single physical laptop.

compiler_baselines.note: sequential + OpenMP baselines reused unchanged from Assignment 3 (same source, same flags)
compiler_baselines.gcc: gcc (MinGW-W64 x86_64-ucrt-mcf-seh, built by Brecht Sanders, r1) 16.1.0

power_plan.benchmark_plan: High performance (8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c); switched by run_benchmark4.py before the campaign and restored afterwards
power_plan.why: Balanced throttled the BLAS kernel by ~2-3x, which would have confounded the Spark/C/numpy comparison

protocol.weak_scaling_rule: n_total = n_1 * p^(1/3) so that n^3/p (work per worker) stays constant
protocol.worker_definition: 1 worker = 1 standalone worker process (1 JVM, 1 core); drivers and masters are separate processes; 1 physical machine
protocol.distributed_variant: row-block partition of A + B replicated to every worker with sc.addFile; numpy/BLAS matmul per block
protocol.min_batch_note: 0 forces batch = 1 in the C bench mode, so every measured batch is exactly one multiplication
protocol.timing_boundary: additive driver phases per repetition: t_e2e = t_stage_a (split + serialize A) + t_action_job (dispatch, transfer, compute, collect) + t_assemble (rebuild C)
protocol.startup_excluded: t_startup (SparkSession + executor launch) and t_replicate (addFile + forcing job that materialises B everywhere) are one-time per application and reported separately; the per-task Python-worker respawn is NOT excluded, because on Windows a fresh worker process is started for every task
baselines: numpy_sequential: same BLAS kernel, 1 process, 1 thread (isolates distribution overhead from kernel speed)
matmul3_simd: Assignment 3 OpenMP/SIMD C kernel at p in {1,2,4,8} threads
known_limitations: sc.broadcast is unusable on Windows: PythonBroadcast.readObject moves its temp file into the block manager while the FileOutputStream is still open, and Files.move fails with ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION. Verified against the bundled JDK 21; sc.addFile is used instead (same 8n^2 bytes per worker).

Python workers cannot be reused on Windows: PythonWorkerFactory.releaseWorker only requeues when useDaemon is true, which needs os.fork(). Every task pays a fresh python.exe + import pyspark.worker + numpy.
The i7-1355U (2 P-cores + 8 E-cores, 15 W) caps useful parallelism at ~1.9x: measured 1-thread 65 GFLOP/s vs 8-thread 121 GFLOP/s on the same BLAS kernel.
All workers are processes on ONE physical machine, never separate nodes.
protocol.validation: distributed C vs matmul3_seq C on identical inputs, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-12 (numpy/BLAS summation order differs from ikj)
protocol.inputs: data/inputs/A_n.bin, B_n.bin (same generator/seed as Assignments 1-3, byte-identical where sizes overlap)
